=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves are attached at successive nodes along the stem, alternating sides; no paired or whorled arrangement visible)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): distal (leaves are spaced out along the stem, not clustered at nodes)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single, undivided blade)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): toothed, serrate (margins have small, sharp, forward-pointing teeth along the edge)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (longer than wide, tapering to a point at apex, broad at base)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tapering to a sharp point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (base is broadly curved, not tapering or heart-shaped)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein runs from base to apex, with secondary veins branching off laterally)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, closely spaced, numerous (secondary veins are clearly visible and run parallel to each other, close together)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny, glabrous (surface appears smooth and glossy, no visible hairs)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or trichomes on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is short, leaf blade appears nearly sessile or with very short stalk)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petiole is round in cross-section, no wings or grooves visible)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears firm and rigid, with brownish bark, typical of young woody plant)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem surface)
    19. Stem color: brownish-green (stem is greenish-brown, with some reddish-brown tones)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (surface appears smooth without prominent ridges or lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules visible at leaf base)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex exudate visible upon inspection)

    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils visible)
F. Notes: Some leaves show small holes and brown spots, likely due to minor damage or aging; overall plant is a young seedling growing on forest floor with leaf litter; no flowers or fruits visible. The leaf shape and margin are consistent across all images, confirming observations. The petiole is very short, contributing to the nearly sessile appearance of the leaves.
